Arun Kumar P.No. 5 Of 18 BK The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with Teena (Dar) vs Arun Kumar(24/20Lc) on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185459878/ 4 reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2024.11.21 Date: 17:06:56 +0530 MACT NO:783/21 Teena v. Arun Kumar P.No. 7 Of 18 BK earned. 14. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 14.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). 14.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities CHARU Digitally signed by CHARU GUPTA Date: 2024.11.21 GUPTA 17:07:06 +0530 MACT NO:783/21 Teena v. Arun Kumar P.No. 8 Of 18 BK (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
texts.facts: 1. The present accident claim is based on a detailed accident report (Dar) filed by the police in terms of provisions of Mv Act. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 24.01.2020, petitioner Teena Yadav aged about 18 years was going towards her home, riding a Scooty bearing no. RJ-14WD-8813 with her cousins brothers Nirbhay(aged7years) and Ranveer(aged 9 years) after picking them from school. At about 1 pm, when she was on 3rd Avenue Road at the first crossing, near Block-13, a Pulse Renault car bearing no. DL-1OQ-5860(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came from her left side, driven in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed and hit the Scooty which the petitioner was riding. As a result all three of them fell from the Scooty and sustained injuries. Driver of the offending vehicle took the injured persons including the petitioner to the hospital. 3. An FIR no.0024 dated 24.01.2020 was registered u/s 279,337 of IPC at PS Lodhi Colony and the matter was investigated. After investigation, a charge sheet was filed before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle(Respondent no.1) while DAR was filed before this Tribunal. Respondent no.1 is driver, Respondent no.2 is owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent no.3 is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. In response to the DAR, Respondent no. 1 and 2 filed their reply denying their fault or liability. It is denied that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving by Respondent no.1. It has been pleaded that in fact the petitioner namely Teena Yadav was triple riding with the other two injured persons, without having a valid driving licence and without the Scooty that she was riding being duly insured. It is therefore that petitioner Teena Yadav was also convicted u/s 3/181,196 & 128/177 of M.V. Act in a kalandra dated 24.11.2021. It has been pleaded that the petitioner was not only driving the Scooty rashly and negligently and at a very high speed but was also grossly negligent in so far as she was riding two minor children on her Scooty and therefore is solely liable to compensate the other injured. It is further pleaded that even the offending vehicle is duly insured. As per reply filed by insurance company, liability is denied on the ground of negligence of the petitioner apparent from the fact that she was triple riding on a Scooty without holding a valid driving licence or wearing helmet. It has been pleaded that since petitioner has also been challaned u/s 128/177 & 129/177 MV Act, she is not entitled to compensation. It is further pleaded that the case is bad for misjoinder and non-joinder of proper parties. 6. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 10.03.2022. Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA OPP. 3. Relief. 7. To prove her claim, petitioner led her evidence by examining herself as PW-1 by way of affidavit as Ex.PW-1/1. As per the affidavit, on 24.01.2020 at about 1.00 PM, she alongwith her cousin brothers was returning back after picking them from school. When she reached at 3rd Avenue Road, Block No.13, offending vehicle bearing no. DL-1CQ-5860, a silver colour pulse Renault came from right side with over speed and hit her Scooty bearing no. RJ-14-WD-8813, as a result she fell down and received injuries. She was 18 years of age at the time of accident. She deposed that she spent Rs.25,000/- on her treatment and special diet. She relied upon DAR as Ex.PW-1/A She was duly cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken.
